scientific: Peromyscus maniculatus (the northwestern forest form; often split as P. keeni on the Olympic coast)

size.note: Head and body 0.08-0.10 m, tail 0.08-0.12 m in the northwestern forest form, mass 0.015-0.03 kg, ears about 1.6 cm. Built at 0.09 m head and body (nose to tail root) and a 0.09 m tail; 0.04 m at the back, 0.049 m to the ear tops; 0.18 m nose to tail tip.

source.title: Deer mouse (variant of the California vole's Meshy mesh)
source.author: variant of microtus_californicus by agent (Claude) for Aaron Brodeur
source.original: the California vole's text-to-3D preview, ai_model meshy-6-lite, triangle remesh to 20,000 faces (the generator gave it a mouse's thin tail and rat-like ears)
source.prompt: (the vole's) A California vole (Microtus californicus), a wild meadow vole, NOT a mouse, NOT a hamster. One adult on all fours in a neutral side-on pose, feet on the ground, head level. Realistic proportions: 17 cm long including a short 4.5 cm tail, stocky cylindrical body, short legs, blunt rounded face, small beady eyes, small round ears almost hidden in fur. Grizzled cinnamon-brown back with darker ticking, grey belly, grey feet, tail dark above and grey below. No whiskers as strands. No base, no ground. Game-ready.

tiers.note: lod0 = body + lofted tail (6 sides x 10 rings, 114) + eyes (16); lod1 = body + tail (4 x 6, 44) + eyes (16); lod2 = body + tail (3 x 3, 15). GLB 163,512 bytes.

rig: Template R as client/assets/vole.glb (tools/build_vole.py) plus a tail part, as client/assets/rabbit.glb writes it: BODY 0 (hindquarters), CHEST 7 (fore body, pivot at the lumbar: lifts to sit up and eat), LEG_A 1 (fore pair, elbows) and HEAD 6 (neck, head, ears, eyes; pivot at the neck) children of the chest, LEG_B 2 (hind pair, stifles), TAIL 3 (the lofted tail, pivot at its root, weight rising from 0 at the root to 1 by 15% along). No TAIL_TIP. extras.rig keys: kind, chest, tail, head, fore, hind, length_m (the vole's plus 'tail'). No skin. The client's vole constants have the tail amplitude at 0 (no tail part): this model needs a constant set with a tail swing.
accuracy_notes: Reads as a deer mouse, not a vole: slim, long-legged, a pointed snout, big thin rounded ears (dusky with a pale rim), big protruding black eyes, a sharp line low on the flanks to a pure white belly, throat, chin, inner legs and feet, grey-brown back darker down the spine, and a long thin sharply bicoloured tail (dark above, white below) drooping toward the ground. Still the vole's body underneath: the rump is heavy (pear-shaped from above) for a deer mouse, and the white flank line climbs onto the back of the haunch. The tail is 3.2 mm thick at the root, so at game distance it is a line. Eyes on lod0 and lod1; lod2 is a 64-triangle body.
